top_story_title: Citrix NetScaler RCE zero-days exploited globally for weeks (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772)
top_story_summary: Citrix has patched eight critical and high-severity vulnerabilities in NetScaler, two of which - CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 - were exploited as zero-days against internet-facing appliances for weeks before fixes existed. CVE-2026-88771 is an improper input validation flaw in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway that allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands. CVE-2026-88772 is an out-of-bounds memory flaw in the same products that can lead to remote code execution or denial of service.
top_actions: Inventory all NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway instances, including HA pairs, cloud-hosted and MSP-managed units; check the Citrix advisory for the fixed release for your branch and upgrade.
Treat any appliance that was internet-facing before the patch as potentially compromised: terminate all active sessions, revoke session tokens and assume stolen session cookies.
Rotate device certificates, admin credentials, API tokens, LDAP/RADIUS service accounts and any secrets stored on the appliance after upgrading - a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
Remove the NetScaler management interface (NSIP/management GUI, SSH, API) from public exposure entirely and restrict it to a dedicated management network.
Review the running config, responder/rewrite policies and virtual server definitions for unauthorized changes, and look for unexpected files or shell accounts on the appliance.
executive_summary: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory corruption, RCE or DoS) were exploited as zero-days for weeks; both are on CISA's KEV list, added 2026-09-27, due 2026-09-30.
Patching is the floor, not the fix: appliances exposed before the patch need session revocation, credential and certificate rotation, and a compromise hunt.
Fixed releases are not stated in this cycle's sources - take the version from the Citrix advisory, not from third-party reporting.
One other collected item concerned AI-themed credential phishing against policy researchers, not network infrastructure, and was dropped.
No defensive AI capability from a network vendor appeared in this window.
key_actions: **Citrix** — Confirm the running NetScaler build against Citrix's fixed-release table and schedule the upgrade now; in an HA pair, upgrade the secondary first and verify config sync afterwards.
**Citrix** — Apply the fix to every unit in the device group, including non-production, DR and MSP-managed appliances - partial coverage leaves the same entry point open.

headlines.title: Week in review: Researcher breaks into Microsoft analytics service, NetScaler RCE 0-day exploited
headlines.summary: Two NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, were exploited as zero-days for weeks before Citrix patched; both are now KEV-listed.
